stage: Current Jupiter keyed/keyless gateway and shared bounded request admission
runtime_requirement: Keep bot/API/UI/training/research stopped. No operator signing, orders, wallet/provider calls, active model fit/promotion or policy activation is authorized by this source stage.
findings: Actual managed get_order/execute_order and buyer/seller route selection incorrectly required a nonempty API key, although the current official gateway supports keyless requests. This is a present source-contract mismatch, not proof that it caused the historical no-buy run.

Default quote, unsigned build and price routes retained Lite gateway dependencies. Official documentation describes progressive Lite retirement and keyless api.jup.ag replacement; it does not establish an exact already-completed global retirement date.

Price had a separate local throttle and persistent secret-bearing session. Main gateway quote/order/build/price requests lacked shared cross-loop admission, while signed execute requires its independent gateway bucket.
implemented: Migrate known Lite and legacy v6 observation/build aliases before the first HTTP request. Use api.jup.ag defaults and retain explicit self-hosted observation/build adapters without forwarding Jupiter credentials. Preserve explicit managed/legacy disable switches and all four managed routers; no operator environment is rewritten.

Permit keyless managed orders/execution and actual buyer/seller route selection. Keep complete original packet/projection/signature/chain proof checks. Do not convert invalid keys, permissions, redirects or gateway failures into anonymous retries or additional signed execute requests.

Use one process-wide threading-locked, cross-event-loop admission manager for keyed/keyless main buckets and independent execute buckets. Default main 0.5/1 RPS and execute20/50 RPS; explicit keyed paid-plan rate selects execute100 RPS. Add pacing, sixty-second sliding windows, a bounded128-ticket priority queue, bounded caller deadlines, cancellation cleanup and redacted counters. Exit probes/orders precede queued entries, generic quotes and background prices; already admitted requests are not preempted.

Observe200/429 remaining/reset headers. Treat reset as an absolute Unix timestamp freeing one slot, not clearing local reservations or expanding quota. Preserve admissions and credentials on auth/permission/server errors. Bound corrupt/server-skew metadata and use conservative missing-header fallback. No execute POST retry.

Move actual managed dispatch-started provenance and original expiry/projection-age checks to immediately before POST, after execute budget waiting. Proved local pre-HTTP budget refusal or pre-POST aging remains a preparation failure; errors after the actual dispatch marker remain uncertain even if their exception type resembles a pre-dispatch failure.

Add per-request scoped credentials, no redirects and sanitized transport diagnostics to quote/build/price. Persistent price sessions carry no API key. Keep existing price-only throttling and observation/fill contracts. Invalid optional transport refuses requests without crashing cold paper imports or initializing a live signer. Correct the public legacy priority-fee example to the documented nested v1 shape; this does not certify full legacy instruction semantics.

limits: Local admission is process-wide only; separate processes, keys/organisations and firewall peers may exhaust provider quota. JUP_API_RPS is operator-declared configuration, not verified plan entitlement. No paid plan is purchased or auto-expanded.

Keyless access permits HTTP requests, not successful production order/node simulation, fresh market depth, wallet capital, timely fills or profitable entry/exit behavior. Provider latency/freshness/access acceptance remains untested while runtime is stopped.

The existing five-second local projection-to-dispatch contract remains enforced after waiting; unsupported, missing or aged observations may legitimately refuse a route. It is not relaxed to generate more trades.
